scope: Juiced state writes retain a private last-committed checkpoint; failed writes restore rejected policy/cache controls and revision. Policy is the sole authority for Hot residency.
ModelManager serializes profile/options writers and keeps changed candidates private until both files commit. This is not P3 crash-consistent multi-file promotion.
Cloud requests capture endpoint, credential, header, permission, wire format and revision together. Combined install/auth publication is coherent, and delayed discovery revalidates before publishing.
Provider-scoped retirement rejects busy workers before commit, gates concurrent acquisition during publication and supports retryable cleanup after committed metadata removal.
Returned native errors and thrown AdmissionError share status/code/retry classification before Ollama/Anthropic formatting.
CI retains native logs and cloud proof artifacts on failure; positive cancellation fixtures use explicit pending-state observation without changing production or negative-test deadlines.

Final ModelManager readers recheck cache validity under the read lock. Options writers resolve the selected recipe inside the writer transaction, and native APIs reject changes since recipe validation.
Supported/downloaded/direct model discovery and the console catalog project the committed execution profile consistently.
Per-model committed policy revisions and exact worker generations order pin, reconciliation and queued unload effects. The Juiced state mutex is never held across those Router calls.
Cache forgetting and pruning commit tombstones before file deletion. Failed metadata publication preserves files; cleanup failure remains retryable across restart.

Portable ordering fixtures cover successful profile/policy races, obsolete queued commands, replacement generations, discovery parity and multi-snapshot failure/retry/restart. CPU fixtures explicitly select CPU before Hot loading.

Router projects committed Juiced residency policy at existing/fresh/retry/restoration publication. Obsolete policy-generated preloads reject before admission and revalidate through startup without holding shared policy locks over slow loading.
Deferred downsizing retains the selected generation and rechecks pin, readiness, activity and current idle duration atomically before maintenance.
Model-options GET/POST/DELETE and dry-run responses derive recipe/profile, saved values and defaults from one native snapshot.

Undeleted cache tombstones retain disk charges. Qualified snapshot writes reserve capacity and headroom before dispatch. Unknown or uncertain writes remain charged; only confirmed completion or exact current-generation stop permits cleanup.

Actual Linux CPU acceptance verifies inference continues while failed cleanup occupies the full snapshot budget, restart cleanup reopens saving, and an incorrect declared write bound invalidates saving without failing inference.

Snapshot publication seals candidate checksum, prior metadata and both file destinations before replacement. Previous files remain owned until new metadata commits, then retain tombstone charges until cleanup succeeds. Restart recovery verifies content outside the shared state lock.

Any observed snapshot write exceeding its declared maximum invalidates further saving, including non-200, malformed, disconnected and delayed responses. Uncertain writes retain disk ownership until exact-generation stop; requalification is explicit.
Dry-run options previews consume the validated normalized mutation, preserving registry defaults when null, empty, auto or minus-one clears an override. Context minus-one remains explicit.

Sealed snapshot recovery restores checksum-verified previous content or commits tracked cleanup for missing/corrupt candidates. A per-publication claim excludes concurrent verification/mutation while hashing stays outside the shared state lock. Unknown unsealed writes still require termination proof.
Save dispatch is recorded by the exchange owner after its cancellation check. Proven pre-dispatch cancellation durably releases unused disk credit in JSON/SSE without unloading the worker.

Accepted credential/auth-mode changes commit a new persistent transition generation before serving. Unchanged restarts retain their namespace; A/anonymous/A and A/B/A do not revive old namespaces. Failed activation leaves the previous configuration and namespace intact.

Chunked imports seal file/checksum/destination/registration intent before rename, serialize finish/cancel/chunk ownership and reconcile restart/retry. ModelManager owns no-overwrite and provenance-based idempotency. Conflicting names remain explicit and can finish under a distinct name. Cancellation commits before cleanup. Completed import replay does not recreate removed models.

ModelManager per-model mutation ownership serializes registration, import publication and removal. Committed publishing intent vetoes native/gateway removal; final publication revalidates provenance. Import no-overwrite protects the full current public namespace, including conflict rename.
Initial/replayed import recipe and purpose normalize to one effective definition. Compact Library controls retry publication, resolve name conflicts and retry cleanup through native endpoints.

Unset/empty admin overrides inherit the regular key before enforcement, identity and epoch activation. Empty credentials never match configured keys. Trusted-LAN and admin-only behavior remain explicit.

Cache-profile qualification parses the actual slot-save argument through the backend argument owner and compares filesystem directories. JSON escaping, unrelated option values and ambiguous duplicate flags cannot qualify storage.
Dynamic BackendOps discovery executes outside shared model cache/options-writer locks. A serialized builder revalidates native invalidation and provider revisions before native cache publication.

Options/profile write snapshots hold per-model and file-writer ownership after discovery, binding the recipe, selection and registry defaults through persistence. Notifications defer until outer mutation ownership releases. Unknown-model import option overlays remain supported.
Directory watcher lifecycle serializes separately; joining a watcher holds no cache lock, and directory/invalidation publication is atomic under the cache owner.

Server terminal shutdown drains native model notifications and retained-job workers before model/provider dependency destruction. Failed construction follows the same cleanup path; terminal watchers cannot restart and the backend process accessor cannot retain a destroyed instance.
HTTP shutdown and startup failure return through Server lifetime teardown. Signal handlers publish atomic intent to a joined native worker; no detached reload callback holds a Server pointer.
